findings.title: Apply website visibility restrictions to website_name
findings.body: website_name is not included in untrusted_attributes, so anonymous viewers receive a TL0 user's website host and same-domain path even when scope.restrict_user_fields? hides website. The updated template also displays this otherwise restricted information. include_website_name does not prevent this: it lacks the serializer hook's trailing question mark and only checks presence. Apply the same visibility restriction as website and cover website_name in the anonymous-user serializer test.

findings.title: Keep the website label synchronized with website edits
findings.body: The label now uses a server-loaded property instead of the computed property that observed model.website. User.save() submits the edited website but only updates bio_excerpt from the response, leaving website_name unchanged. Consequently, an already loaded profile can show the old domain while its link points to the new website; adding or clearing a website also leaves the display stale until the user is fetched again. Update website_name after saving or preserve reactive label computation.

findings.title: Do not hide websites containing non-ASCII URL paths
findings.body: Ruby's URI parser rejects raw non-ASCII characters anywhere in the URL. For a browser-supported website value such as http://example.com/café, this rescue sets website_host to nil, website_name returns nil, and the template hides the website entirely—even when only the host needs displaying. The previous split-based host extraction handled this value. Normalize or escape the URL for parsing rather than treating such a parsing failure as an absent website.

findings.title: Do not treat a shared public suffix as the same domain
findings.body: Removing the first label from equally sized hostnames incorrectly identifies unrelated domains as the same site. For example, an instance at discourse.co.uk and a website at example.co.uk both have three labels, so this comparison matches co.uk and displays the website's full path. Independent sites under github.io have the same problem. The same-domain exception should compare registrable domains or explicitly supported hostname relationships, not merely the remaining labels.
